text:
sam: Quick question — we're getting flaky infra PRs where GH Actions does a post-commit job that expects Terraform outputs to exist, but Atlantis is the source of truth for plan/apply. What do people think about having GH Actions upload the Atlantis plan JSON as an artifact and then a small handshake check so downstream jobs wait for Atlantis to finish planning?

alex: I ran into this last week. Uploading plan.json from atlantis ("atlantis plan -p prod --json > plan.json") and attaching it to the PR works. GH Actions can then download the artifact and read the outputs. Problem: atlantis runs on our GH webhooks so plan timing is async. Need a reliable PR check to know plan finished.

ida: We tried a simple polling check: GH Actions polls the Atlantis server API for plan status. It worked but felt hacky. Better to use GitHub Checks API — Atlantis could push a check once plan completes. Is there an existing integration?

maria: +1 for a checks-based approach. Alternatively GH Actions could wait for the plan artifact to exist in the repo (artifact storage). I've done: 
```yaml
- name: wait for atlantis plan
  uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
  with:
    name: atlantis-plan-prod
    path: ./atlantis
```
But need atlantis to upload with a stable artifact name.

jonathan: To avoid race/apply duplication: keep Atlantis as the only applier. GH Actions should not auto-apply. If GH job needs outputs for k8s templating, read them from the plan JSON (or from a short-lived S3 bucket where atlantis uploads the applied outputs). We use s3://redwood-infra-outputs/{pr}/{workspace}/outputs.json and a signed URL.

sam: Good ideas. Concern: secrets wiring — we use SOPS for secrets and ArgoCD's secret generator expects certain Kubernetes secrets to already exist. If GH job renders k8s manifests using tf outputs + sops-decoded secrets, we must ensure we don't leak anything. Thoughts?

ida: For secrets, keep them in the deployment repo (encrypted). GH Actions can decrypt with KMS if runner is allowed, but better: have atlantis/infra pipeline upload minimal rendered Secret resources to a secure artifact store and mark them ephemeral. ArgoCD sync should be gated behind a canary label.

alex: Another pattern: have the infra repo commit a tiny "manifest refs" file that ArgoCD watches (kustomize: vars from TF outputs). Atlantis only commits this post-apply via a bot user. Then ArgoCD picks up the change and syncs. That way GH Actions doesn't need to do apply; it only runs validations.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Atlantis plan completed for PR #298 (workspace: prod). Plan JSON available at: https://artifacts.redwood.internal/atlantis/298/prod/plan.json :white_check_mark:

jonathan: Nice — infra-bot link is exactly what we need. GH Actions can follow the link or download the artifact. Let's standardize the artifact path and name so workflows are reusable.

maria: Action items i can own: 1) Add an Atlantis step to upload plan JSON artifact to internal storage with path pattern `atlantis/{pr}/{workspace}/plan.json`. 2) Update GH Actions job to wait/download that artifact before doing any tf->k8s translation. 3) Ensure GH Actions never calls terraform apply.

sam: Sounds good. Can we also add a quick lock to avoid double-apply if somebody manually runs atlantis apply at the same time as an automated job? Maybe a DynamoDB lock or a GitHub check flag that indicates "apply in progress".

ida: We already have a lightweight DB lock used by the deploy pipeline. Reusing that is easiest. I'll add a small step in Atlantis that sets a lock key `infra:apply:{workspace}` and clears on completion. GH Actions should respect the lock before proceeding.

alex: I'll open a draft PR for the GH Actions waiting job and a Terraform snippet to emit plan JSON. Will tag you all for review.

sam: Thanks — huge improvement. If we get the artifact + check pattern in place we should eliminate most flakes where manifest rendering runs before plan exists. :rocket:
